snapshots.name: Woland
snapshots.subtitle: A foreign professor of black magic
snapshots.body: An elegant, mocking stranger with mismatched eyes who has arrived in Moscow from abroad, talks as if he had met both Kant and Pontius Pilate, and has a contract to give performances at the Variety Theater. He seems to know a great deal about the people he meets.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Koroviev
snapshots.subtitle: A lanky man in a checked jacket, one of Woland's companions
snapshots.body: Long, thin and jeering, in a little jockey cap and a pince-nez with one lens missing, he calls himself a former choirmaster and keeps turning up at the side of the foreign professor. He talks a great deal, mostly in mock servility, and nothing he says can be taken at face value.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Behemoth
snapshots.subtitle: An enormous black cat in Woland's retinue
snapshots.body: Huge as a hog, black as soot and with a cavalryman's mustache, he walks on his hind legs, talks, drinks vodka and tries to pay his fare on the tram. He is the troupe's clown and its most enthusiastic troublemaker.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Azazello
snapshots.subtitle: A short, red-haired member of Woland's retinue
snapshots.body: Short, extraordinarily broad-shouldered and fiery red-haired, with a fang sticking out of his mouth, he speaks bluntly through his nose and has no patience with pretence.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Hella
snapshots.subtitle: Woland's maid
snapshots.body: A young woman who opens the door of the apartment where the foreign artiste is staying, wearing nothing but a little lace apron, a white headpiece and golden slippers. A livid scar marks her neck.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: The master
snapshots.subtitle: Ivan's nameless neighbor at the clinic, the author of a novel about Pilate
snapshots.body: A historian by training who won a hundred thousand roubles, gave up his museum job and wrote a novel about Pontius Pilate. He will not give his name, calls himself only a master, and keeps a black cap with an M that a woman sewed for him.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Margarita Nikolayevna
snapshots.subtitle: The master's beloved
snapshots.body: Thirty years old, childless, beautiful and clever, married to a prominent, kind specialist and wanting for nothing, she has not known happiness since she married at nineteen. She has had no word of the master since he disappeared and cannot tell whether he is alive.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Natasha
snapshots.subtitle: Margarita's housemaid
snapshots.body: The pretty housemaid in Margarita's home, who looks after her mistress and notices her moods.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Nikolai Ivanovich
snapshots.subtitle: Margarita's neighbor on the lower floor
snapshots.body: A respectable resident of the ground floor of the house where Margarita lives.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Latunsky
snapshots.subtitle: A literary critic
snapshots.body: A Moscow literary critic. Ivan's neighbor at the clinic says he wishes it had been Latunsky under the tram instead of Berlioz.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Aloisy Mogarych
snapshots.subtitle: A journalist who befriended the master
snapshots.body: A man Woland's people bring, in his underwear and clutching a suitcase, before the master and Margarita. He has some connection with the master's old basement rooms.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Ivan Bezdomny
snapshots.subtitle: A young Moscow poet who writes under the pen name Bezdomny
snapshots.body: Ivan Nikolayevich Ponyrev is a broad-shouldered, tousle-haired young poet in a checked cap who writes under the pen name Bezdomny. He has written an anti-religious poem on commission for Berlioz's magazine.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Mikhail Alexandrovich Berlioz
snapshots.subtitle: Chairman of Massolit and editor of a literary magazine
snapshots.body: Short, plump, bald and well read, in huge horn-rimmed glasses, he edits a thick literary magazine and chairs the board of Massolit, one of Moscow's largest literary associations.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Annushka
snapshots.subtitle: A Moscow woman
snapshots.body: A woman the foreigner at Patriarch's Ponds mentions in passing: she has already bought sunflower oil, he says, and spilled it.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Ryukhin
snapshots.subtitle: A poet from Griboyedov House
snapshots.body: A poet from the writers' house who helps carry Ivan out of Griboyedov's and goes with him to the clinic.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Archibald Archibaldovich
snapshots.subtitle: Manager of the Griboyedov restaurant
snapshots.body: The host of the writers' restaurant, who runs it with quiet authority and an eye for trouble.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Professor Stravinsky
snapshots.subtitle: Head of the psychiatric clinic
snapshots.body: The courteous, observant doctor in charge of the new clinic outside Moscow, who listens to his patients without arguing with them.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Praskovya Fyodorovna
snapshots.subtitle: A nurse at the clinic
snapshots.body: The plump nurse on Ivan's ward, who brings him paper and a pencil stub when he asks for them.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Styopa Likhodeyev
snapshots.subtitle: Director of the Variety Theater
snapshots.body: Stepan Bogdanovich Likhodeyev shares apartment No. 50 on Sadovaya Street with Berlioz. He wakes there one morning with a fearful hangover and no memory of the day before.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Rimsky
snapshots.subtitle: Financial director of the Variety
snapshots.body: Grigory Danilovich Rimsky is a dry, careful man in horn-rimmed glasses who keeps the theater's money.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Varenukha
snapshots.subtitle: Administrator of the Variety
snapshots.body: Ivan Savelyevich Varenukha runs the theater's day-to-day business.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Georges Bengalsky
snapshots.subtitle: The Variety's master of ceremonies
snapshots.body: A clean-shaven compère in a rumpled tailcoat, well known to all Moscow, who introduces the acts at the Variety.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: The master of ceremonies
snapshots.subtitle: A stage compère
snapshots.body: The man who introduces the acts on a stage. The novel uses the title for more than one compère; at the Variety it belongs to Georges Bengalsky.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Arkady Apollonovich Sempleyarov
snapshots.subtitle: Chairman of the acoustics commission
snapshots.body: The evening's guest of honor at the Variety, chairman of the Acoustics Commission of the Moscow theaters. He sits in box No. 2 with two ladies and wants the tricks exposed.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Nikanor Ivanovich Bosoy
snapshots.subtitle: Chairman of the tenants' association at No. 302-bis Sadovaya
snapshots.body: The harassed head of the building where Berlioz lived. Since the editor's death he has been besieged by tenants who want the dead man's rooms.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Pelageya Antonovna
snapshots.subtitle: Nikanor Ivanovich's wife
snapshots.body: She keeps house for the chairman of the tenants' association and has his dinner waiting when he gets home.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Kanavkin
snapshots.subtitle: A man in Nikanor Ivanovich's dream
snapshots.body: Nikolai Kanavkin is called up onto the stage in the strange theater of Nikanor Ivanovich's dream, where the audience is pressed to hand over its hidden currency.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Prokhor Petrovich
snapshots.subtitle: Chairman of the Entertainment Commission
snapshots.body: The chairman of the Entertainment Commission, whose voice is heard giving someone a dressing-down behind his office door.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Vasily Stepanovich Lastochkin
snapshots.subtitle: The Variety's accountant
snapshots.body: A diligent accountant who finds himself the senior man at the Variety the morning after the performance.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Maximilian Andreyevich Poplavsky
snapshots.subtitle: Berlioz's uncle from Kiev
snapshots.body: An economic planner from Kiev who arrives in Moscow after receiving a strange telegram about his nephew's death.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Andrei Fokich Sokov
snapshots.subtitle: The Variety's barman
snapshots.body: The man who runs the theater's refreshment bar.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Professor Kuzmin
snapshots.subtitle: A Moscow physician
snapshots.body: One of Moscow's best-known specialists in diseases of the liver.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Baron Meigel
snapshots.subtitle: A caller at apartment No. 50
snapshots.body: A baron who telephones the apartment where the foreign artiste is staying and is told the artiste will be glad to see him.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Frieda
snapshots.subtitle: A guest at the ball
snapshots.body: A woman with gloomy, imploring eyes among the guests, who begs the hostess to remember her name.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Abadonna
snapshots.subtitle: One of the powers who serve Woland
snapshots.body: A figure whose work Woland shows Margarita on his globe, where a distant war is being fought.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Pontius Pilate
snapshots.subtitle: The Roman procurator of Judea
snapshots.body: Rome's governor of Judea, who comes out onto the colonnade of Herod's palace in a white cloak with a blood-red lining. He hates the smell of rose oil and the city of Yershalaim, and on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan he has a crushing headache and a prisoner to judge.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Yeshua Ha-Notsri
snapshots.subtitle: A wandering philosopher from Gamala
snapshots.body: A poor, beaten young man of about twenty-seven, brought bound before Pilate. He says he has no permanent home and is alone in the world, and he calls everyone, including the men who beat him, a good person.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Levi Matvei
snapshots.subtitle: Yeshua's only follower
snapshots.body: A former tax collector who threw his money into the road to follow Yeshua and writes down what Yeshua says on a goatskin parchment. Yeshua says he writes down things that were never said.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Aphranius
snapshots.subtitle: Head of the procurator's secret service
snapshots.body: A middle-aged officer with a pleasant face, who keeps his small eyes half-hidden under heavy lids. He knows what happens in Yershalaim and reports it to Pilate in private.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Judas from Kiriath
snapshots.subtitle: A young man from Kiriath
snapshots.body: A young man of Yershalaim. Yeshua tells Pilate that Judas was kind and inquisitive and invited him home.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Joseph Caiaphas
snapshots.subtitle: The high priest and president of the Sanhedrin
snapshots.body: The acting head of the Jewish council in Yershalaim, which has condemned Yeshua and must decide which prisoner to release for the feast.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Mark Ratslayer
snapshots.subtitle: A Roman centurion
snapshots.body: A giant of a centurion whose face was disfigured in battle. Pilate sends for him to teach a prisoner how to address the procurator.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Niza
snapshots.subtitle: A young woman of Yershalaim
snapshots.body: A young married woman of Yershalaim who knows Aphranius.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Bar-Rabban
snapshots.subtitle: A prisoner in Yershalaim
snapshots.body: A man Pilate names while questioning Yeshua; his case also comes before the procurator that morning.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Dismas
snapshots.subtitle: A prisoner in Yershalaim
snapshots.body: A man Pilate names while questioning Yeshua; his case also comes before the procurator that morning.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Gestas
snapshots.subtitle: A prisoner in Yershalaim
snapshots.body: A man Pilate names while questioning Yeshua; his case also comes before the procurator that morning.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.

snapshots.name: Banga
snapshots.subtitle: Pilate's dog
snapshots.body: The dog Pilate calls for when his headaches overwhelm him.
snapshots.editorialBasis: Reviewed baseline identity at first mention; no concealed identity or later plot development.
